headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill mandates that large energy users, such as data centers, bear the costs of their increased electricity demand and associated grid infrastructure, rather than socializing these costs across all ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocacy groups, Governor Spanberger.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial users.
news_headline: Virginia Shifts Data Center Energy Costs to Large Users.
news_summary: New legislation, including HB 1393, requires data centers and other large energy users consuming 25 MW or more to pay for the increased generating capacity they demand. This measure aims to prevent these costs from being passed on to other customers, protecting residential ratepayers from higher utility bills.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates increased reporting of water consumption by data centers to enhance transparency and inform future water resource management and environmental regulations.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, water conservation advocates, local governments, Governor Spanberger.
news_headline: Virginia Legislates Data Center Water Use Transparency.
news_summary: Virginia passed legislation, including SB 553, requiring data centers and other industrial facilities to submit annual water consumption estimates. This aims to provide clarity on water usage for rezoning and special use permit decisions, enhancing transparency and oversight of the industry's water footprint.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill grants localities more authority to regulate the siting of data centers and impose noise limits, addressing community concerns about development impacts.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents, local governments, environmental groups.
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry.
news_headline: Virginia Strengthens Data Center Siting and Noise Regulations.
news_summary: New legislation, including HB 153, enhances local control over data center development by requiring sound assessments near residential areas and schools. It also allows localities to demand impact assessments on water, agriculture, and historic sites before project approval.
